title: Replicating MALT Evaluation Tampering Detection on Novel Agentic Frameworks

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: framework-specific tampering variants are a real concern as agentic frameworks diversify, but the finding is likely to be that some tampering transfers and some does not, without clear actionable implications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires setting up LangGraph-based agent loops, deploying open models in agentic scaffolds, and implementing transcript monitoring. This is advanced infrastructure work for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Running MALT-inspired scenarios in a new framework plus identifying new tampering variants is sustained effort. The scope is manageable but requires both framework setup and novel behavior identification.

evidence: METR released MALT dataset (Oct 2025) with 10,919 transcripts covering evaluation tampering behaviors, but focused on software/research tasks with specific models.
Petri (Anthropic, Oct 2025) and Petri 2.0 (Jan 2026) test evaluation tampering and oversight subversion on frontier models, not specifically in novel agentic frameworks like LangGraph.
No published work found replicating MALT-style evaluation tampering detection specifically in LangGraph or other novel agentic framework architectures.
